overall.summary: Every stated number, closed form, coverage and preservation figure reproduces, but the daytime leaf calls evening minutes a minor partner of the heavy-use unit when at heavy day use they move the predicted risk from 5% to 93%; the service-call reading misses the 0-2 call plateau and 'hardly for heavy users' holds only above about 50 dollars.

findings.statement: a heavy-use unit (2470) ... that grows with the day charge (and a little with evening minutes)
findings.check: probe with evening minutes and charge set to consistent pairs at a day charge of 48 dollars; training subgroups by day charge and evening minutes (fewer than 4 service calls)
findings.evidence: Evening use is a major partner of the heavy-use unit, not a small one. Typical customer at a day charge of 48 dollars: 5.1% at 100 evening minutes, 45.7% at 200, 93.0% at 300. In the data (fewer than 4 calls), day charge 40-45 dollars: mean predicted risk 5.9% (n=56, outcome 5.4%) with under 150 evening minutes against 53.8% (n=50, outcome 62.0%) with 250 or more; day charge 45-50: 14.1% (n=30) against 81.1% (n=30). Per sd the closed form gives evening minutes 0.514 inside the chain against about 1.06 for the day charge: half as strong, not 'a little'.

findings.statement: a heavy-use unit (2470) ... pushed down by customer-service calls
findings.check: node values of 2470 on the training rows and in probes
findings.evidence: Unit 2470 is on for 3307 of 4000 customers, including every customer with 0, 1 or 2 service calls whatever the day charge (392 of 472 with a day charge of 20 dollars or less); at 10 dollars and 1 call it is 0.53. Its on/off state is set by service calls (concept probe: calls AUC 0.98, r2 0.33). It is a 'few service calls' gate whose call threshold rises with day and evening use, rather than a heavy-use unit; as a result the first two service calls add nothing for any customer.

findings.statement: the predicted risk rises steeply with calls, 1.4% at 1 call, 16.1% at 4, 73.1% at 6 and 98.4% at 8 calls
findings.check: probe grid day charge x service calls 0-9
findings.evidence: The numbers reproduce, but the shape is a threshold, not a steady steep rise: at 30 dollars the risk is 1.4%, 1.4%, 1.4% at 0, 1, 2 calls, then 4.8%, 16.1%, 41.9%, 73.1%. The same holds at every day charge (10 dollars: 4.3%, 4.2%, 4.1%, then 13.6% at 3 calls). The onset moves with the day charge (3 calls up to 35 dollars, 4 at 40, 5 at 45, 7 at 50, 8 at 55). The hypothesis does not say that 0 to 2 calls make no difference.

findings.evidence: Holds only for the very heaviest users. Only 16 training customers have a day charge of 55 dollars or more (above the 99th percentile, 51.78). findings.statement: The main interaction is between two children: the heavy-use unit of daytime_use loses about what the service-call edge adds, so service calls raise the risk of light and average daytime users much more than that of heavy ones
findings.evidence: The cancellation is real (2.59 x 0.677 = 1.75 per sd against the edge's 1.73) but it applies to every customer while unit 2470 is on, which is all customers with up to 2 calls; heavy users differ only in keeping it on to more calls (V2, V3). The self-probe numbers reproduce (1.4%, 41.9%, 90.9%, 90.3%; with an international plan 15.6%, 90.4%, 99.2%, 99.2%).

findings.statement: Its main effect is a U-shape in daytime charge ... calls matter for light and average users but hardly for heavy users until the very highest call counts
findings.evidence: The high end of the 'U' depends as much on evening use as on the day charge (V1); evening minutes are not named as a driver anywhere in the record, and the service-call effect is described without its 0-2 call plateau. Same applies to record.summary's opening ('mainly from daytime use, customer-service calls and the two plans') and record.clinical_terms ('heavy daytime users'): the profile is heavy day plus evening use.

daytime_use.why: The light-use unit is a clear 'low day charge adds risk' term, but the second exit is mainly a gate that switches off with service calls, and its heavy-use side depends on evening minutes about half as much as on the day charge, which the reading calls 'a little'.

service_calls.why: More service calls raise the predicted churn risk, with an extra hinge for 7 or more calls; the reading misses only the 0-2 call plateau created by the daytime gate.

night_use.why: A small rise in risk with night use, steeper below about 125 minutes, from two nearly cancelling copies of one column.

evening_calls_hinge.why: Customers with more than about 115 evening calls get a slightly lower predicted risk; confirmed by node counts and probe.

intl_charge_hinge.why: International charges above about 2.70 dollars raise the predicted risk steadily; confirmed by probe.

direct_usage_terms.why: An international plan raises and a voice-mail plan lowers the predicted risk, plus small usage terms; confirmed by probe and subgroups.

state_single_units.why: Per-state constant offsets for Connecticut, Maryland and Wyoming (Georgia's unit dead), each confirmed to fire exactly for its state.

state7_chain.why: A Washington DC offset that fires for exactly the 73 DC customers and lowers their predicted risk.

state42_night_calls_chain.why: Its last unit can never switch on, so it has no effect; there is nothing to read.

direct_location_terms.why: Per-state constants on small groups; Hawaii and Vermont stand out, the rest are small unnamed offsets.
